```shiploop-state
{
  "evidence_refs": [
    "Original request and sentence index S1–S11",
    "Host-provided installed-skills list",
    "README.md",
    "package.json",
    "src/text.js",
    "test/text.test.js"
  ],
  "headline": "Intake mapped the requested helper changes, delivery boundary, and discovery questions.",
  "outcome": "done",
  "question_categories": [
    {"applies": "yes", "id": "K1"},
    {"applies": "yes", "id": "K2"},
    {"applies": "yes", "id": "K3"},
    {"applies": "yes", "id": "K4"},

    {"applies": "yes", "id": "K10"},
    {"applies": "yes", "id": "K11"},
    {"applies": "yes", "id": "K12"}
  ],
  "questions": [
    {
      "id": "Q1",
      "category": "K1",
      "question": "How will the user invoke the helper against real exports, and what representative record shape demonstrates it is usable?",
      "changes": "The consumer example, boundary test, and delivery instructions.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first checks the repository and available export context; if none identifies another entry point, assume a CommonJS helper called by the user's existing Node.js export code.",
      "blocks": "A claim that a particular real-export workflow has been verified; nothing else if the default proceeds."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q2",
      "category": "K2",
      "question": "What behavior of the old trim helper must the record-wide helper preserve, including its field selection and treatment of the input record?",
      "changes": "The scope and compatibility requirements for the new helper.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first looks for the old helper, its callers, and tests; if unavailable, assume a shallow transformation of a record's own enumerable string-keyed fields, preserving keys and returning a new record.",
      "blocks": "A claim of compatibility with the old helper; implementation may proceed under the recorded default."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q3",
      "category": "K3",
      "question": "What are the established name, export, input and output shapes, and error behavior for the record-wide helper?",
      "changes": "The public API and contract tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first checks old helper conventions and consumers; if unavailable, assume a named CommonJS export called squashRecord that accepts a plain record and returns a new record with squash applied to each field; propagate TypeError for invalid field values.",
      "blocks": "Finalizing the record helper contract until discovery or the default is recorded."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q4",
      "category": "K4",
      "question": "How should the helper handle invalid record inputs, arrays, nested values, empty records, symbols, inherited fields, and nullish field values?",
      "changes": "Validation rules and edge-case tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first checks the old helper and real record shapes; otherwise accept plain records, return an empty record for an empty input, process own enumerable string-keyed fields shallowly, map nullish field values to empty strings, and throw TypeError for non-string, non-nullish field values and invalid record inputs.",
      "blocks": "Finalizing edge-case tests until discovery or the default is recorded."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q5",
      "category": "K5",
      "question": "Does the old helper mutate its input or preserve special properties, and are records shared across callers?",
      "changes": "Mutation, property handling, and isolation tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first checks the old helper and callers; otherwise assume no mutation, no shared persistent state, and no special treatment of prototypes or property descriptors.",
      "blocks": "A compatibility claim about mutation and special properties; nothing else if the default proceeds."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q6",
      "category": "K6",
      "question": "Which Node.js versions and dependency constraints apply to the intended consumer?",
      "changes": "Syntax, dependency choices, and runtime verification.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first checks project and consumer configuration; if absent, use the existing CommonJS and node:test conventions without adding dependencies and verify on the available Node.js runtime.",
      "blocks": "A claim of compatibility with unspecified Node.js versions; nothing else if the default proceeds."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q7",
      "category": "K7",
      "question": "Is there an established record-helper module or export seam that consumers require?",
      "changes": "The location and export path of the new helper.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first checks existing modules and consumers; otherwise place the helper alongside squash in src/text.js and export it there.",
      "blocks": "Finalizing the public entry point until discovery or the default is recorded."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q8",
      "category": "K8",
      "question": "Which tests establish the existing string behavior and the record helper's real consumer boundary?",
      "changes": "Regression and acceptance coverage.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first inspects existing tests and consumers; otherwise extend test/text.test.js with node:test and node:assert, run npm test, and cover string preservation, nullish values, invalid types, and the recorded record contract.",
      "blocks": "Verification against an undiscovered consumer boundary; repository-level tests proceed under the default."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q9",
      "category": "K9",
      "question": "Where must the completed code be available for tomorrow's export trial, and is there a release or integration step?",
      "changes": "The delivery target and any required access or release step.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first checks repository and consumer delivery context; if no deployed target is identified, deliver the updated source checkout and usage information to the user without assuming a release.",
      "blocks": "A claim that an unidentified export environment has received the change; source delivery can proceed."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q10",
      "category": "K10",
      "question": "What workload and acceptable time or memory bounds make one million records practical?",
      "changes": "Performance verification and any justified optimization.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first checks representative record sizes, environment, and existing performance expectations; otherwise favor a straightforward implementation, avoid speculative optimization, and do not invent a numeric performance guarantee.",
      "blocks": "A quantified million-record performance claim; functional work can proceed."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q11",
      "category": "K11",
      "question": "Can the requested review and improvement skills be invoked in the delivery environment, and what evidence will expose compatibility or export-data risks early?",
      "changes": "The review sequence, risk checks, and completion evidence.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first resolves the host's code-review and improve skills and checks representative records; the host describes code-review as reviewing a diff or pull request and improve as iterating until only trivial changes remain. Do not claim either ran unless its invocation and result are available.",
      "blocks": "Completion of the requested skill-based review and improvement if the named skills cannot be invoked; other discovery can proceed."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q12",
      "category": "K12",
      "question": "What does the Orchard style guide require for doc comments, and where is its authoritative copy?",
      "changes": "Doc-comment wording and conformance verification.",
      "route": "research",
      "default": "Discovery first checks installed skill references and repository documents, then authorized team or internal sources and search; if no authoritative guide is found, use the existing concise comment style provisionally without claiming Orchard compliance.",
      "blocks": "A verified Orchard-compliance claim and any guide-dependent final comment decisions; other work can proceed."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q13",
      "category": "K12",
      "question": "What do 'usual whitespace', 'dogfood-able', and 'the old trim helper' mean for this consumer?",
      "changes": "Whitespace tests, the usability boundary, and record compatibility.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first checks installed skill references, repository behavior, old helper and consumer evidence, then authorized sources and search; absent contrary evidence, 'usual whitespace' means the current JavaScript trim and regular-expression whitespace behavior (high confidence), 'dogfood-able' means callable by the user on real exports (medium confidence), and 'old trim helper' means a prior record-wide helper whose exact contract is unknown (low confidence).",
      "blocks": "Claims about the old helper and actual export workflow; the recorded defaults permit other work."
    }
  ],
  "summary": "S1 [fact]: Scope is the records-helper repository. S2 [fact]: squash must return an empty string for null and undefined while retaining TypeError for numbers and objects. S3 [fact/open Q2–Q5]: Add a record-wide squash helper modeled on the old trim helper, whose exact contract discovery must establish. S4 [fact/assumption/open Q1, Q9]: Make the helper usable by the requester on real exports for the intended trial tomorrow, assuming the source checkout is the delivery target unless discovery identifies another target. S5 [fact/open Q11]: Use an installed review skill for edge cases, with code-review acceptable, then run improve on its findings; neither skill was run during intake. S6 [fact]: Keep any regular expressions readable in one pass. S7 [fact/assumption/open Q13]: Preserve the current JavaScript whitespace behavior as the best reading of usual whitespace. S8 [fact/open Q12]: Follow the Orchard doc-comment guide once discovery locates it; existing comment style is only a provisional fallback. S9 [fact]: Preserve squash's existing string behavior exactly, including trim and whitespace collapse. S10 [fact]: Add tests in the existing node:test and node:assert style. S11 [fact/open Q10]: Aim for practical processing of one million records without speculative optimization or an invented performance threshold. Discovery leads [hints, not verified sources]: the old trim helper and its consumers, representative export shapes and runtime, the host's installed code-review and improve skills, and the Orchard guide in authorized team/workspace channels, internal documentation or private repositories; no owner, specific channel, private repository, or guide location is identified. Keep sensitive locators in an authorized private store, never KNOWLEDGE/. Run boundary [fact]: this unattended stage only reads workspace files, changes nothing, starts no server, and implements nothing. Delivery boundary [assumption]: the updated source must be usable from the user's checkout after final return; an isolated run's source checkout remains at its snapshot until then, and a deployed target would contain the outcome only after release. No interactive product or prior run is identified; no release target is established."
}
```

commands.command: /bin/zsh -lc 'for f in README.md package.json AGENTS.md; do if [ -f "$f" ]; then printf '"'\\n%s\\n' \""'$f"; cat "$f"; fi; done'
